name: Mauve rose
lede: Mauve rose is a dusty, greyish pink-purple on the warmer side of the [[mauve]] family, dated to Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature and confirmed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955 as a close match to its own "light grayish purplish red" block.

sections.title: One block, many brand names
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system places Mauve rose in block 16, only 1.6 units from that block's center, a close fit [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary and the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 attach a long chain of near-synonyms to the same block, among them Vinaceous, Candida, Grey Pink and Mauve Orchid, each a separate trade name landing close to the same point [1]. The books in color-kb have no entry for "Mauve rose" itself [4].

In the ColorHub library the point is also carried, with no measurable difference, as Vinaceous-Lilac (ΔE 0.0) [1][3]. Its nearest distinct neighbor is [[anemone]], 2.6 units off and "almost the same" by our graph's own description [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Mauve rose is rare in our archive: 22 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.1 percent, as photographed [2]. Where it appears, it keeps unusually close company with plain [[mauve]], turning up on the same canvases far more than chance would predict [3]. Counts are computed matches on varnished, photographed paintings, not pigment identifications [2].

questions.q: In the ColorHub library, Mauve rose and Vinaceous-Lilac are:
True or false: Mauve rose is one of the colors our archive finds most often.

openers: Mauve rose shares its ColorHub library point exactly with a second trade name, Vinaceous-Lilac.
